problem:
Determine a set of parametric equations, defined for $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),$ that generate a vertical parabola that has its vertex at $(0,0)$ and which passes through the point $(-2,4).$ Express your answer in the form $x=2pt,y=p{t}^{2},$ where $p$ is a constant.

$x=$
{{field-1}},
$\,y=$
{{field-2}}
worked_solution:
The parametric equations of a vertical parabola  that has its vertex at $(0,0)$ are

$$
x=2pt,\,y=p{t}^{2},
$$

where $p$ is constant.

Since the parabola passes through $(-2,4),$ we can substitute $x=-2$ and $y=4$ into the standard parametric equations to obtain a system of equations. This gives

$$
{\begin{aligned}-2=2pt \\ 4=p{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the first equation for $t,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}-2 & =2pt \\ t & =-\frac{1}{p}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into the second equation and solving for $p,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}4 & =p{(-\frac{1}{p})}^{2} \\ 4 & =p\cdot \frac{1}{{p}^{2}} \\ 4 & =\frac{1}{p} \\ p & =\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

$$
x=2(\frac{1}{4})t,\,y=(\frac{1}{4}){t}^{2},
$$

which simplify to

$$
x=\frac{1}{2}t,\,y=\frac{1}{4}{t}^{2}.
$$
